adjudication_findings.claim: eq-5 and eq-17 combine definitions with theorem conclusions.
adjudication_findings.paper_locus: Eq. 5, p.4 line 155; Eq. 17, p.12 line 597
adjudication_findings.reason: Both displays do define and assert. prop-4.2 depending on eq-17 and lem-2.1.i depending on eq-5 is circular at row level though not in the paper. Split; adjudicates against r3's alternative, see R3-DEP-04.

adjudication_findings.claim: Split claim-minimax-mu into generic minimax, Forrelation instantiation and r-fold bound.
adjudication_findings.reason: Lemma 4.1 is not used for existence of mu, and Lemma 2.1(i) discharges only L<R(P). Modified: instantiation lands in prop-4.2 through hP, so two rows rather than three: claim-minimax-mu (generic) and new claim-address-guess. Also drop the needless 1<=L.

adjudication_findings.claim: The planted theorem should be generic in P and C and take 1<=L<=m, L<R(P).
adjudication_findings.reason: The proof uses circuit correctness only. A family must then instantiate the same efficient circuit for both bounds, since F depends on C.

adjudication_findings.claim: prop-4.2 drops lem-2.1.i and eq-17; claim-Y-values drops lem-2.1.iii; claim-tail, claim-numeric lose edges.
adjudication_findings.reason: The concrete row needs lem-2.1.i. Resolved by a new prop-4.2-generic carrying r3's shape. claim-Y-values keeps the dependency as spec only. With the eq-17 split the tail edges are harmless.

statement: For each fixed integer k>=2 and every sufficiently large power of four m, R(F_{k,m}) > G=floor(mL/100), with L=floor(m^{1-1/k}/(log_2 m)^2).
